why: NIGHT-7 T1 established this programme's citation failure mode, and it is not fabrication. Five external reviews quoted numbers that were REAL and published, stripped of the qualifier that made them true: a long-short alpha applied to a long-only book, a rebalancing premium measured against buy-and-hold quoted as alpha against a rebalanced benchmark, a 131.83% return quoted without its Sharpe of 0.31. Prose cannot enforce a qualifier. This file makes the qualifier a REQUIRED FIELD, so a citation without one fails to load.

verdict_codes.V-C: verified with a correction to the number
verdict_codes.V-M: the number is real but was used misleadingly
verdict_codes.U: could not verify — may not be quoted

citations.claim: up to 188 bps/month alpha from year-over-year filing text change
citations.source: Cohen, Malloy & Nguyen, Lazy Prices, JF 75(3) 2020, 1371-1415 (NBER w25084)
citations.qualifier: LONG-SHORT: shorts 'changers' and buys 'nonchangers'. Sample 1995-2014. The figure is the spread, not a long-leg return.
citations.why_not: the book is long-only. Aegis's own §28 finding is that 99.9%/88% of a spread lives in the short leg a long-only book cannot hold; the derived long-leg prior is roughly x0.30.

citations.claim: professional managers show skill in buying; selling underperforms random selling
citations.source: Akepanidtaworn, Di Mascio, Imas & Schmidt, JF 78(6) 2023, 3055-3098
citations.qualifier: 783 portfolios, avg $573M, 4.4M trades, 16 years. Mechanism is asymmetric attention. The DIRECTION is verified; the '90-120bps/day earnings-season' magnitude circulating in reviews is NOT in the reachable text.
citations.how: supports studying exit rules at all. It does NOT license a specific exit magnitude, and NIGHT-7's G7 result (-3.08%/yr for a trailing stop) is evidence about vehicles, not about the paper.

citations.claim: about 4% of stocks account for all net stock-market wealth creation
citations.qualifier: 4.3% of 25,967 CRSP PERMNOs, measured against one-month T-bills over the full 1926-2016 life of each stock. 42.6% of stocks beat T-bills over their lifetime, so the common 'half fail to beat T-bills' understates it (57.4% fail).
citations.how: argues against concentration in a long-only book and for breadth — consistent with NIGHT-1's own measured finding that breadth beats concentration.

citations.claim: implementation decisions beyond the style choice are themselves alpha-generating
citations.qualifier: qualitative claim about implementation, not a quantified edge. The paper does not license a bps estimate.
citations.how: the product track's honest framing: craftsmanship and discipline, never a 'beats S&P' claim.

citations.claim: tax-loss harvesting is worth 1.10%/yr gross, 0.85%/yr under the wash-sale rule
citations.qualifier: 1.10 / 0.85, NOT the 1.08/0.82 that circulated. Assumes 15%/35% long/short-term rates, 1926-2018, top-500 cap universe. It is a TAX effect available only to a taxable account, and depends on the investor's bracket.
citations.how: relevant to the product track for taxable accounts only; it is not alpha and may never be added to a backtested excess return.

citations.claim: specialised ETFs lose about 30% risk-adjusted over their first five years
citations.qualifier: driven by OVERVALUATION OF THE UNDERLYING AT LAUNCH, explicitly not by fees or hedging demand. The finding is about entry timing into hyped themes, not about thematic exposure being bad.
citations.how: inverts the naive reading of thematic strategies: the lesson is that narrative-salient ENTRY is the problem. Any thematic work here must test entry timing, not theme selection.

citations.claim: a new factor needs t > 3.0 given the mining history of the literature
citations.qualifier: the hurdle is for a claim of a NEW FACTOR against the published factor zoo. It is not the hurdle for an implementation choice inside an already-accepted factor, and it is not a portfolio-adoption rule.
citations.how: the bar the survivor is measured against; it is the reason a t of 2 is not a discovery here.

citations.claim: the Deflated Sharpe Ratio controls for multiple testing, non-normality and sample length
citations.qualifier: DSR is a PROBABILISTIC-SHARPE statistic against a selection-adjusted benchmark Sharpe. It is NOT a posterior probability that true alpha is positive, and NIGHT-7 stated it that way in error. GATE-M1 additionally measured DSR>=0.95 as nearly powerless on this programme's own ladder, so it may not be re-armed as a kill gate.
citations.how: reported beside, never above, an empirical selection bootstrap.

citations.claim: a bootstrap test of whether the best model in a specification search genuinely beats a benchmark
citations.qualifier: the null concerns the BEST MODEL ENCOUNTERED IN THE SEARCH over a FIXED set of alternatives. It does not reproduce an adaptive search whose later branches depended on earlier outcomes, so applying it to recovered finished strategies yields a LOWER BOUND on search burden.
citations.how: T4b's method; registered as a fixed-alternative lower-bound audit for exactly this reason.

citations.claim: SPA improves on White's Reality Check by studentising and using a sample-dependent null
citations.qualifier: the improvement comes specifically from the studentised statistic plus recentring that stops poor alternatives setting the null's scale. A demeaned-max bootstrap without that recentring is NOT SPA and may not be labelled as such.
citations.how: required in T4b because this candidate set contains cost-destroyed books at t -8.4.

citations.claim: the stationary bootstrap resamples weakly dependent stationary series with geometric block lengths
citations.qualifier: assumes stationarity and weak dependence. Candidates with different inception dates are not a stationary panel; their missing history must be MASKED, never zero-filled, or the fabricated flat months shrink variance and inflate the winner.
citations.how: T4b's resampling scheme, with the same block index applied across all candidates to preserve the cross-section.

citations.claim: anonymised headlines outperform originals in-sample
citations.qualifier: in-sample. The interpretation is that the DISTRACTION effect of the entity name exceeds the look-ahead gain, particularly for larger companies. It is not evidence that anonymisation removes look-ahead.
citations.how: supports entity masking as useful; NIGHT-7 established it is NOT sufficient, because date memory survives it.

citations.claim: GPT-4 achieves 60.35% directional accuracy on one-year-ahead earnings vs 52.71% for analysts
citations.qualifier: on STANDARDISED AND ANONYMISED financial statements, versus the MEDIAN analyst one month post-release. It is an EARNINGS-DIRECTION task, not a return-prediction task, and it is on par with a purpose-trained ML model rather than beating one.
citations.how: supports the LLM as an extractor/forecaster of INTERMEDIATE quantities. NIGHT-3 separately measured that LLM ordering earns no role in stock selection here (M1 t 0.04, M2 t 0.93).

citations.claim: firm-level political risk measures are freely downloadable as extractor ground truth
citations.source: firmlevelrisk.com (Hassan, Hollander, van Lent, Tahoun), fetched live
citations.qualifier: free historical download covers 2002-2021q2 only, >11,000 firms, 81 countries. Current data is paywalled via NL Analytics. Ground truth for a REPLICATION test, not a live feed.
citations.how: the cheapest available Layer-1 extractor validation; nothing in the LLM programme is worth building until Layer 1 is calibrated against it.

citations.claim: reported LLM trading advantages deteriorate under broader cross-section and longer horizons
citations.qualifier: 20-year multi-source benchmark with survivorship, look-ahead and data-snooping mitigation, 100+ symbols. The finding is about published LLM STRATEGY claims, and reports LLMs as overly conservative in bull and overly aggressive in bear regimes.
citations.how: independent corroboration of NIGHT-3's local negative result.

citations.claim: 131.83% accumulated return on DJIA constituents
citations.qualifier: AT SHARPE 0.31, which is worse than passive. Quoting the return without the Sharpe inverts the paper's meaning. A review used it as evidence of success; with its qualifier it is evidence of the opposite.
citations.why_not: the number is a cumulative return over an unstated benchmark-free window with a sub-passive Sharpe. It licenses nothing.

citations.claim: rebalancing is worth more than 100bps annualised
citations.qualifier: measured against BUY-AND-HOLD over a 5-year horizon for S&P 500 stocks. It is the volatility-pumping / diversification bonus, NOT alpha against a rebalanced benchmark.
citations.why_not: the Aegis benchmark is CRSP VW total return, which is not a drifting buy-and-hold basket. The premium is already inside the benchmark and cannot be claimed on top of it.

citations.claim: parametric look-ahead survives prompting; date-keyed memory is measurable
citations.qualifier: LAP is a DATE-ONLY recall query: materially positive in-sample, collapsing to about zero after the training cutoff. FinCAD cuts in-sample backtest returns by up to 67.1% on MEMORISED DATES while leaving 2025 out-of-sample within Sharpe 0.10 of baseline.
citations.how: the correction to NIGHT-1. That experiment measured identification of the COMPANY (0/240); LAP measures memory keyed on the DATE. Masking is necessary, not sufficient — CANON 13.

citations.claim: point-in-time-trained LLMs show lookahead bias is modest
citations.qualifier: the finding cuts AGAINST alarm, not for it: real-time outputs achieve Sharpe comparable to a much larger Llama, which the authors read as lookahead bias being modest. Frequently cited here as if it demonstrated the opposite.
citations.how: tempers, and does not license, the leakage panic; the FinCAD/LAP date-memory result is the one that changes our procedure.

citations.claim: per-idea basis-point estimates offered in external reviews (e.g. '120-310bps vs AVUV', '+1.0-1.5% expected edge', '105 high-turnover ideas', '$935k trading cost')
citations.qualifier: no source, not derivable from anything in this repository. Our comparable measured figures are $602,509 (NIGHT-6 clock) and $743,599 (NIGHT-7 trailing stop).
citations.why_not: invented precision. Such items may be carried as hypothesis LABELS and never as estimates.
